payload.rationale: Observed: as of 2026-09-19, the official Dune: Part Three site advertises a December 18, 2026 North American release, December 16 international, and early-access screenings December 14–15, with Warner Bros./Legendary and Villeneuve credited. The film reportedly wrapped principal photography in 2025 and has held its December 2026 IMAX date for a long time; three months out, with early-access screenings already scheduled and marketing underway, a tentpole delay would be highly unusual. Base rate: major studio tentpoles that are still confirmed on their date ~90 days prior are delayed only a few percent of the time absent extraordinary events (pandemic, strike, catastrophic post-production failure). Warner Bros. has strong incentive to keep the Christmas corridor and IMAX commitments. Too-high consideration: the schedule is already locked with exhibitors and premium-format bookings; the true probability may be closer to 1–2%. Too-low consideration: VFX-heavy films occasionally slip late (e.g., studio corporate turmoil at Warner Bros. Discovery, a competitive shuffle, or a last-minute date move of even one week would count as YES); unresolved resolution ambiguity (e.g., how a move to a later day in the same week or an earlier date is treated) adds a little tail risk. I also cannot verify current news between the site retrieval and the deadline. Net estimate ~4%.
limitations: No browsing; cannot confirm post-production status or any news after 2026-09-19.
Advertised release date is not a guarantee; some site sections had placeholder text.
No fitted historical base rate; estimate relies on general knowledge of tentpole scheduling behavior.
Contract nuances (e.g., partial or regional date shifts) may affect settlement in ways not fully captured.
